text.p: The copper market showed signs of tightening again on Thursday and prices rallied after a week when prospects had seemed at most flat.
Commodities across the board, outside oil and precious metals, saw only moderate levels of activity.

But the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper market at one moment almost moved back to the recent backwardation, when prompt material commands a premium over forward months. Traders said this reflected tighter prompt supply and the possibility that new data on Friday may show a continuing decline in world stocks held in LME-supervised warehouses. LME three month copper rose to $1,944 per tonne which was up $22 from Wednesday and well above last week's $1,850 low. Floor traders said the near-term direction for copper remained unclear following the collapse earlier this year of what traders saw as the end of a bid by Sumitomo Corp of Japan to defend a strong price.
But they said the market seemed tighter with a lot of physical business this week.
Chicago benchmark wheat futures were little changed around $4.30 a bushel.

Coffee futures were also little changed ahead of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meeting that starts on Friday. Delegates will review export figures and commitments against a backdrop of leftist guerrilla attacks in Colombia, the world's second largest producing nation.
